questions.q: What did doctors wrongly advise for decades, according to the summary?
a: Switching to low-fat foods
Eating more red meat
Avoiding all vegetables
Fasting one day a week
questions.why: The first lesson says fat is recovering its reputation after years of misplaced low-fat advice.

questions.q: Which foods does the summary list as rich in omega-3 fats?
a: Mackerel, salmon, sardines and grass-fed meat
Olive oil, avocados and mixed nuts
Bread, pasta and white rice
Coconut oil, butter and full-fat yogurt
questions.why: The first lesson says omega-3s support memory, brain cell function and mood.

questions.q: How does the summary suggest you start producing ketones?
a: Fast for 16 hours now and then
Skip dinner every single night
Eat only protein for a week
Exercise before breakfast daily
questions.why: The second lesson says a 16-hour fast still leaves eight hours in the day for eating.

questions.q: Why are ketones described as a cleaner fuel than glucose?
a: They are made in fewer steps and leave less waste
They carry far more calories per gram
They are absorbed directly from the air
They never affect insulin levels at all
questions.why: The second lesson compares the switch to going from a gas car to an electric one.

questions.q: What does the Genius Plan ask you to avoid during its first 14 days?
a: Processed carbs, sweeteners, gluten and soft drinks
All fats, including olive oil and nuts
Fruit, vegetables and eggs
Meat, fish and dairy
questions.why: The third lesson says clearing these from your pantry reduces brain inflammation before carbs return.
